verify_text:
protocol.py: VERIFIED against plate map dil-01. 12 of 12 wells hold what the plate map says.
  Destination: NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 3). Reading of the request:
    row A; first point is 1:2; excess removed from the last well.

Labware for the technique (Serial dilution): nothing to flag.

Where every liquid ended up (ul):
  liquid                             declared delivered in source elsewhere    lost
  drug                                 1000.0     100.0     900.0       0.0     0.0
  pbs                                  1500.0    1100.0     300.0       0.0   100.0
  Note: 100.0 ul of pbs is lost: it left the deck inside a tip that was thrown away.

Prep sheet: what to put on the deck before the run.
  slot labware                               well  liquid                       load at least  declared
  2    Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 1.5  A1    drug                                 100.0    1000.0
  4    NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL          A1    pbs                                 1200.0    1500.0
  Tips: 1 from Opentrons OT-2 96 Tip Rack 300 µL in slot 1.
  'Load at least' is what the robot draws. Add the dead volume of your tube or reservoir.

This checks the logic of the protocol: what goes where, and how much. It does not check the
  physics: whether a viscous liquid is pipetted accurately, or a drop stays on a tip.

intent.variant: row A; first point is 1:2; excess removed from the last well

notes: 100.0 ul of pbs is lost: it left the deck inside a tip that was thrown away.

check_text:
protocol.py: 6 biology problems (1 error, 3 warnings, 2 notes).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 5 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
   line 27:  p300.mix(20, 5)
   At line 27 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 5 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this
   line did it 240 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the
   wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The
   simulator passes the move. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot
   3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [92a356f55b4f]

2. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: pbs (well A1 in slot 4)
   line 23:  p300.aspirate(100, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 23 the tip went into pbs (well A1 in slot 4) while it still carried drug (tube A1
   in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it
   in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong
   there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that were given
   that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in the stock is
   no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 23 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [b75b80580965]

3. WARNING WELL-CAPACITY: More liquid than the well is rated for: 200 ul against 100 ul, 12
wells
   line 26:  p300.dispense(100, well)
   At line 26 the robot filled wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3
   past the 100 ul the maker states for it (this line did it 12 times), reaching 200 ul,
   under the 217 ul the well holds to its rim. Above the stated maximum the liquid climbs
   the wall and wets the seal, a tip going in displaces it over the edge, and the volumes
   still add up on paper, so the plate map does not see it and the simulator says nothing.
   Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Use labware rated for the volume, or scale every volume down so the fullest well
   stays under the stated maximum with room to mix.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [3c693324e350]

4. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: Mixing too weak to stir 12 wells: 20 × 5 ul in 200 ul
   line 27:  p300.mix(20, 5)
   At line 27 the tip mixes wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3 with
   20 strokes of 5 ul in a well holding 200 ul (this line did it 12 times). 20 strokes of 5
   ul move 0.5 of the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the
   mixing work). Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV
   where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated,
   and in a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (160 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 160,
   well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [650841f1b5fc]

5. NOTE CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: drug (tube A1 in slot 2)
   line 25:  p300.aspirate(100, source)
   At line 25 the tip went into drug (tube A1 in slot 2) while it still carried pbs (well A1
   in slot 4) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it
   in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong
   there. The protocol does not draw from it again, so this run is not harmed, but what is
   left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 25 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [77fef177cc47]

6. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No blank on a dilution series: 12 wells of drug
   line 26:  p300.dispense(100, well)
   At line 26 the robot starts a dilution series of drug in NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR
   Full Skirt (slot 3): 12 wells at 12 concentrations, each level about 2 times weaker than
   the one before. No well on this plate holds pbs with no sample, so there is no blank: the
   curve has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be
   told from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in
   slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Add a well of pbs alone, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [7049b315c99c]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
